prediction.likelyOutcome: Universal's recovery in this unlawful detainer trial depends almost entirely on whether the trial court accepts the application-of-payments theory as satisfying CCP §1161(2)'s one-year notice requirement — a genuinely close question that survived demurrer but faces real headwinds from strict-construction doctrine and the notice's failure to specify the rental period. If Universal prevails on that threshold issue, it likely recovers the $65,989 in back rent plus substantial accruing holdover damages and a fee award; if it loses, the unlawful detainer action fails in its entirety and Universal is left, at best, to pursue rent (and a fresh, properly-scoped notice) outside this proceeding.

issues.label: Three-Day Notice Timeliness Under CCP §1161(2) / Application-of-Payments Theory
Tenant's Discount/Credit Defense (2022 Rent Reduction Promise)

outcome.description: After a three-day court trial the trial court entered judgment for the landlord on July 3, 2025 awarding possession, $65,989 in past-due rent (the amount demanded in the notice) and $123,111 in holdover damages, $189,100 in total; no fee award is stated in the opinion. The Court of Appeal reversed, holding the three-day notice void because the unpaid rent fell due more than one year before service, and remanded for entry of judgment in favor of the tenant.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: the three-day notice was void, so the landlord takes nothing in this action.
